answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network enforces quadratic stake burning for every registered identity. An attacker attempting to scale counterfeit nodes faces superlinear cost: deploying n agents requires burning n² tokens, turning an ivory tower of duplicate keys into an unsustainable drain. While a single ferrous hardware node can sustain minimal base fees, clustering identities drives burned capital toward an exponential zenith, guaranteeing severe economic friction.
